title: Positive and negative numbers in context
summary: Partners describe real situations with opposite quantities (sea level, temperature, bank accounts, yardage), choose which direction is positive, and say exactly what 0 means each time.

standard.text: Understand that positive and negative numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values; use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts, explaining the meaning of 0 in each situation.

discourse: Describe a situation with a pair of opposite quantities and state which direction is positive and which is negative.
Define 0 for the specific context (sea level, 0 degrees Celsius, an account with no money in it, the line where the play started) instead of saying 0 means nothing.
Report a signed number with its unit and reference point so a listener can picture it: 18 feet below sea level, not just negative 18.
sentence: Representation sentences: −12 represents 12 feet below sea level; +50 represents a deposit of 50 dollars.
Signed numbers read aloud as negative five for a value or position, keeping minus for subtraction.
Contrast with while and but: While the diver is below sea level, the bird is above it.
word: Opposite word pairs that signal sign: above/below, gain/loss, deposit/withdrawal, rise/fall, warmer/colder.
Opposite as a math noun (the opposite of 7 is −7) and as an everyday adjective (the opposite side of the street).
Reference-point words: sea level, zero, freezing point, starting line, balance.

contentObjective: Students will use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities with opposite directions or values in real-world contexts and explain the meaning of 0 in each situation.
languageObjective: Students will describe opposite quantities using ___ represents ___ above/below ___ and explain what 0 means in each context with a reference-point noun.

L1-2: Zero means ___. (Word bank: sea level, freezing, no money, start)
L3-4: In this situation, positive means ___ and negative means ___.
Here, 0 stands for ___, so a number below 0 shows ___.
L5-6: I chose ___ as the positive direction because ___; the opposite, ___, is negative.
Although both numbers have the same distance from 0, ___ and ___ describe opposite ___.
Zero is not the absence of a quantity here; it is the reference point where ___.

vocabulary.definition: a number less than 0, written with a − sign
a number the same distance from 0 on the other side, such as 7 and −7
the average height of the ocean's surface, used as 0 for elevation
vocabulary.morphology: level and nivel share a Latin root (libella) but do not look alike

vocabulary.definition: how high or low a place is compared with sea level
money put into an account; shown with a positive number
money taken out of an account; shown with a negative number
to stand for or show something

activity.title: Opposites Gallery
steps: Sketch four situations across the board, each beside a vertical number line marked from −30 to 30: a diver and a bird over the ocean, a thermometer, a bank account, a football play.
For each situation, Partner A chooses the positive direction and says it with a frame; Partner B says what 0 means in that situation. They write both on paper.
Partners write one signed number for the situation and its full description (−18 represents 18 feet below sea level). Move to the next situation after about 2 minutes.
Back at seats, partners solve the problems below, reading every signed number aloud as negative or positive, not minus.
Share: three pairs read what they wrote for the same situation, and the class compares how each pair defined 0.

problems.prompt: A diver is at −18 feet. A bird is flying 25 feet above sea level. How many feet apart are they vertically?
At noon the temperature was 5°C. At midnight it was −3°C. How many degrees did the temperature fall?
A football team loses seven yards on a play. Write the signed number in words and explain what 0 means.
problems.answer: Negative seven yards; zero means the ball stayed at the line where the play started, with no gain and no loss.

warmup: Say a word and have partners answer with its opposite as fast as they can: above (below), gain (loss), deposit (withdrawal), rise (fall), warmer (colder), forward (backward). Then each pair picks one pair of opposites and tells which one they would make positive and why.
